title: Let thoughts pass like buses
description: You do not have to board every thought that arrives; watching them pass, without chasing or fighting them, is the heart of mindfulness.

body.heading: Not every thought needs a passenger
paragraphs: The mind produces thoughts the way a street produces buses: constantly, in all weathers, whether or not anyone is waiting. Some are useful. Many are old routes — the worry bus, the self-criticism bus, the 3 a.m. replay service. We tend to board automatically, especially the loud ones, and ride them for miles.
Mindfulness offers a different relationship: stand at the stop, watch the buses arrive, read their destinations, and choose — more often than you might expect — to let them go past without you.

body.heading: Watching without boarding
paragraphs: In practice it sounds like this: a thought arrives (“I am going to mess this up”), and instead of arguing with it or obeying it, you note it — “there is the worry bus” — and return your attention to the breath, the task, the conversation. The thought may circle the block and return. Note it again. Buses are patient, but so can you be.

This is not suppression. You are not pretending the thought did not come, or wrestling it out of your head. You saw it clearly. You simply declined the ride, which is a different and much more peaceful skill.

body.heading: Why it helps beyond meditation
paragraphs: The bus stop turns out to be a useful place all day long. The irritating comment does not have to become an hour of rehearsed comebacks. The catastrophic headline does not have to become your afternoon. Each declined ride is a small recovery of your own attention and mood.

Some buses, of course, carry things that genuinely need you — a real problem asking for a plan, a feeling asking for care. Board those deliberately, at a time you choose. The practice is not avoidance. It is the difference between being driven by your thoughts and deciding which ones get to drive.

takeaway: Read the destination, wave it past, and keep your attention for the buses you choose.
